stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and no existing spec. Complex feature spanning GO, UP, MX locales/brands requires full elaboration (openspec) to define AC and technical depth, followed by hardening (speckit) for testability, security, and edge cases. Both agents assigned with openspec running first.

agentContributions.notes: Previous output rejected for empty ACs and description containing implementation instructions. Rewrote description to state WHAT (real-time preview without reload), removed HOW (SDK integration details, useContent hook reference). Derived ACs and VCs from the description since original ACs were empty. All VCs are framed at the boundary — given a mocked Contentstack client — because Contentstack services are unreachable at test time.

Openspec provided empty ACs, so all 11 criteria are newly derived from the story description and title. I could not review the contents of the five files listed in technicalNotes (useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx), which limits my ability to identify edge cases tied to existing code patterns — for example, how the context provider handles re-renders or how the link component behaves under preview mode. AC-5 and AC-6 address error handling for connection failures and malformed params. AC-7 addresses security by ensuring no preview connections are made when preview is inactive. AC-8 addresses cleanup/teardown. AC-9 and AC-10 address accessibility of the preview state. AC-11 addresses a common edge case with real-time updates (rapid successive changes causing stale renders). I refined AC-3 from 'without requiring a full page reload' to 'without triggering a hard browser navigation event (beforeunload)' for testability. I refined AC-11 from 'without intermediate flicker or rendering artifacts' to 'within one render cycle and does not display stale intermediate states' for measurability.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Openspec and speckit both ran, but their contributions appear contradictory: openspec claims it 'Derived ACs and VCs from the description,' while speckit states 'Openspec provided empty ACs, so all 11 criteria are newly derived.' This suggests openspec's AC derivation was not persisted or not visible to speckit, meaning openspec may have added little meaningful value beyond description cleanup. Speckit carried the spec work — deriving 11 ACs covering error handling (AC-5, AC-6), security (AC-7), cleanup (AC-8), accessibility (AC-9, AC-10), and edge cases (AC-11), plus refining AC-3 and AC-11 for testability/measurability. However, speckit could not access the five referenced source files (useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx), limiting its ability to identify edge cases tied to existing code patterns. For a complex feature spanning GO, UP, MX locales/brands, no story split was proposed by either agent — a split may be warranted given the cross-brand scope. Human review needed to: (1) reconcile the agent contradiction, (2) verify the 11 ACs against actual source code patterns, (3) evaluate whether a story split is appropriate for the multi-locale/multi-brand scope.
